svg.title: Chapter 3 diode pump power scaling
svg.desc: A comparison of the 19 kilowatt one joule case and two 40 watt arrays producing 4.2 millijoules ideally or about 3 millijoules with 71.4 percent delivery.

g.data-original-text: <text x="600" y="70" text-anchor="middle" class="text">η = 0.35, τp = 150 μs</text>
g.title: η = 0.35, τp = 150 μs

g.data-original-text: <text x="165" y="202" text-anchor="middle" class="text">Eout = 1 J / pulse</text>
g.title: Eout = 1 J / pulse

g.data-original-text: <text x="992" y="226" text-anchor="middle" class="text">× 150 μs = 1 J</text>
g.title: × 150 μs = 1 J

svg.text: Case B: two 40 W end-pump arrays

g.data-original-text: <text x="165" y="387" text-anchor="middle" class="text">2 × 40 W = 80 W</text>
g.title: 2 × 40 W = 80 W

g.data-original-text: <text x="560" y="387" text-anchor="middle" class="text">0.35 × 80 W × 150 μs</text>
g.title: 0.35 × 80 W × 150 μs

svg.text: The 3 mJ estimate includes an unstated practical loss factor.
